# CLI development conventions

Command implementation details and CLI interaction patterns. For installed command usage, run `entire agent-help`; this reference is for changing the implementation.

Repository paths in code spans are relative to the repository root unless stated otherwise.

### Command Layout

The visible CLI is organized around a set of noun groups plus a small set of
top-level verbs. The groups are the canonical home for each verb. Newer
experimental command families are discoverable through `entire labs` and
their canonical paths are always runnable.

Experimental commands are gated by a build-time visibility flag (the
`cmd/entire/cli/experimental` package): they are shown — grouped under an
"Experimental commands:" help section — in developer and nightly builds, and
hidden in stable release builds. Visibility is toggled by `experimental.Visible`
(default `"true"`), which GoReleaser stamps `"false"` only on stable tags
(`.Prerelease` empty); nightly (`vX.Y.Z-nightly.*`) and local builds leave it at
the default. Register a command as experimental with `experimental.Register(parent,
child)` instead of `parent.AddCommand(child)`. Gating only controls visibility —
the commands are always runnable in every build.

- `session` (alias: `sessions`): `list`, `info`, `tokens`, `stop`, `attach`, `adopt`, `resume`, `current`.
  `resume` with a branch arg switches to it and resumes its session; with no arg
  it opens an interactive picker of stopped sessions (across all worktrees),
  resolving each to its branch and pointing at the owning worktree when the
  branch is checked out elsewhere. Resume keeps an existing local session log
  as-is by default (`--force` overwrites it from the checkpoint).
  `adopt` moves an active session from another repo or worktree into the current
  worktree and resets target-local checkpoint bookkeeping so future commits link
  to the adopted session from the new location.
  `current` and a bare `tokens` answer "which session is running this command?"
  through `strategy.ResolveCallerSession`, not "which state file moved last" —
  see [Resolving the calling session](caller-session-resolution.md#resolving-the-calling-session).
- `checkpoint` (aliases: `cp`, `checkpoints`): `list`, `explain`, `tokens`, `search`, `delete`.
  `delete` is user-owned in `agent-help` (agents must not run it unprompted) and
  confirms through `confirmControlPlaneDeletion`; see
  [Deleting a Checkpoint](../architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md#deleting-a-checkpoint).
  `explain` also takes a forge-qualified `--repo` (`gh/<owner>/<name>` or
  `et/<project>/<name>`), the drill-down for a cross-repo `search` hit: it
  reads the checkpoint from that repo's entire-api cell over
  HTTP (`/repos/{repo_id}/checkpoints/{id}` plus `.../transcript/raw`) rather
  than fetching git objects, so a foreign checkpoint never enters this repo's
  object store, ref namespace, or `tokens profile`. It takes a full checkpoint
  ID or a full commit SHA — the SHA is resolved through
  `/repos/{repo_id}/commits/{sha}/checkpoints`, the cross-repo stand-in for the
  local `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer read; zero linked checkpoints is an error,
  and several is an error that names them, unlike the local path which reads
  the first trailer — and a pushed checkpoint; prefixes are rejected. `--commit`
  is accepted with a full SHA only; `--session`, `--search-all`, and `--generate`
  are rejected with it, and naming the current repo is a no-op that falls
  through to the local path. See `checkpoint_api_reader.go`
  (`apiCheckpointReader`, which implements the two checkpoint reader tiers and
  deliberately not `Writer`) and `explain_repo.go`.
  For a local checkpoint, `explain --json` also lists the subagent task records
  stored at `tasks/<tool_use_id>/` under `tasks` (metadata only), and
  `--transcript --task <tool_use_id|agent_id>` streams one subagent's stored
  transcript; both read through `checkpoint.TaskReader`. The cell does not
  serve task records, so under `--repo` the `tasks` key is omitted (not
  reported empty) and `--task` fails with `ErrTaskRecordsUnsupported`.
- `agent`: bare opens the interactive agent selector, plus `list`, `add`, `remove`
- `configure`: bare prints help and a hint pointing at `entire agent`; flags
  manage non-agent settings (telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy
  options, summary provider). Agent CRUD lives under `entire agent`.
- `auth`: `login`, `logout`, `status`, `contexts`, `switch`, plus
  `token` (prints the active control-plane bearer to stdout for scripting/curl;
  honors `ENTIRE_TOKEN`, else the refreshed active-context login JWT). That
  token is also accepted directly at every entire-api cell (e.g.
  `https://aws-us-east-2.api.entire.io/api/v1`), so `token --jurisdiction
  <slug>` is deprecated: the flag stays registered but hidden and fails with
  a migration hint. `auth status` takes no positional
  arguments (`auth status sessions` is refused rather than silently read as the
  default view). It shows the caller's
  home jurisdiction. A login served by a core
  outside that home region reaches `--json` as `foreign_region` and is not
  called out in the text view: the note that used to sit there existed mostly
  to explain the display name and email a foreign core withholds, neither of
  which this view renders any more, and what remained restated the
  `jurisdiction` row beside it. It reports a count of active
  sessions rather than the list — `--sessions` prints the full table, and
  `--json` reports the same facts without the text view's collapse; timestamps
  stay RFC3339 there, since the relative form the text view shows is a reading
  aid. A second count row, `available contexts`,
  does the same for saved logins and replaces the trailing "N login contexts
  saved" sentence. **Both count rows are dropped at exactly one**, and with the
  context count goes the `context` row naming the active login. Both of those
  rows exist to say "this login, not the others", so both wait until there are
  others: a sole login is not a choice, and describing it as one costs two lines
  to tell the reader nothing they can act on. The **login server** is held to the
  same test: the `context` row appends the host only when the saved logins are
  spread across more than one server, because logins that all sit on one server
  are told apart by their names and the host they share names none of them. A
  sole login therefore shows neither row, and `--json` still carries `server`
  for anyone who needs it. ENTIRE_TOKEN mode is the one place the host is stated
  outright, having no context to carry it. The sole session is likewise
  already described by the verdict line's expiry. The session half
  additionally requires that sole session to have been
  *identified* as the caller's: without a `fid` match there is no expiry on the
  verdict line to stand in for it, and dropping the row would leave the default
  view with no count, no expiry and no route to `--sessions` — while the one
  session listed is the login that replaced yours, which is the one worth
  looking at. That window is reachable whenever a family is revoked inside its
  access token's lifetime: `resolveStatusTarget` falls back to the stale bearer,
  `/me` honours it, and `fid` names a family the listing no longer holds. That
  state is named rather than left to be inferred — `! this login was ended
  elsewhere and cannot be renewed`, with the verdict line carrying the *bearer's*
  remaining life instead of a session lifetime, since with nothing left to renew
  it that is when the user is logged out (`login_revoked` / `token_expires_at`
  in JSON; `expires_at` stays absent, no session having been attributed).
  What settles it differs by listing. **Zero sessions settles it alone**: the
  endpoint includes the caller's own session — that is how a matched `fid` finds
  itself — so none listed means none exist, the caller's included, and no
  truncation explains zero. **With sessions listed**, absence is the only
  evidence, so a `fid` must have actually named something; a core too old to
  mint one is evidence of nothing and stays quiet. Do not gate this on the
  refresh having failed: that only becomes known when a refresh is *attempted
  and fails*, and a token still far from expiry is returned without contacting
  the server, so requiring it left the notice silent in the commonest case —
  every session revoked while the current bearer still had hours to run. Zero sessions still reports, being a contradiction worth seeing.
  `logout --everywhere` is offered **only alongside the table**: it ends every
  session at once, browser logins included, and in the collapsed view those
  sessions are a count the reader cannot inspect. It is named as a flag and
  never sized by a number: `logout` sweeps every saved login on every login
  server, while the rows on screen are one server's, so a count there would
  understate what the command destroys. The whole logout hint is
  withheld once a login is known revoked — any session still listed belongs to
  the login that replaced this one, so there is nothing here worth ending, and
  the notice above already names `entire login` as the action.
  The verdict line's deadline is tense-checked before it is printed: a lapsed
  instant renders as a flat `expired` rather than `expires 19h ago`, which would
  contradict the "Logged in" beside it, and an unreadable one is dropped rather
  than echoed mid-sentence (the session table still shows it verbatim in a cell
  of its own, and `--json` carries it untouched). The `--sessions` table's
  `EXPIRES` column is held to the same tense rule and for a sharper reason: its
  heading supplies the verb, so a cell reading `19h ago` says "expired" only by
  implication, which a reader scanning the column will not pick up. `CREATED`
  and `LAST USED` keep the plain relative form, the past being the tense they
  report. Because that deadline is the
  sole-session row's whole premise, the drop is gated on it having actually
  rendered — a session whose `expires_at` is empty or unparseable keeps its
  count row, or the default view would carry no session information at all.
  The drop-at-one collapse is text-only — `--json` never applies it. What the
  JSON does omit is anything it could not determine, which is why
  `active_sessions`, `available_contexts` and `sessions` are **pointers**:
  absent means "not known", never zero. An unreadable listing omits
  `active_sessions` while a real zero emits `0`; ENTIRE_TOKEN mode omits
  `available_contexts`, never having read contexts.json, while every other path
  emits its genuine count; and `sessions` is emitted whenever `--sessions`
  reached the listing, as `[]` when empty, so a satisfied request stays
  distinguishable from the default where the key is absent. Paths that return
  before the listing — not logged in, env token, a failed fetch — omit it
  along with the rest. `env_token` and `token_source` are the exception: where
  the bearer came from is settled before `/me` is consulted, so they are emitted
  even for a bearer `/me` rejected — a script told only `logged_in:false` could
  not otherwise see that `ENTIRE_TOKEN` supplied the token and is still winning
  over every stored context. Every runtime failure reachable once `--json`
  is set likewise prints an envelope carrying `error`, so `--json | jq
  .logged_in` parses: a hard fetch failure (network, DNS, 5xx), an unresolvable
  target (malformed `ENTIRE_TOKEN`, unreadable `contexts.json`, unknown
  `--context`) and the TLS refusal on an `http://` login server all route
  through one helper. A usage error is the deliberate exception: `auth status
  --json sessions` is refused by `cobra.NoArgs` before `RunE` runs, so it exits
  non-zero with empty stdout and a suggestion on stderr. The command keeps its
  non-zero exit and prints nothing further to stderr. The JSON carries the provider-qualified
  `user` and deliberately not a split `handle`/`provider`: one field beats two a
  caller has to rejoin. **Identity is split across providers**, so the view takes
  whichever half each one has. GitHub supplies a human handle
  (`github:gtrrz-victor`); Google supplies a display name and a handle
  minted as `google-<subject id>`, which would qualify to `google:google-100…`
  — the provider twice. How each provider's handle is shown and typed is owned
  by `providerIdentity` (`provider_identity.go`): GitHub handles pass through
  unchanged (so a user genuinely named `github-foo` keeps that name), while
  Google's render as `google:<subject id>`. A `name` row
  carries the display name, and earns its line only where the handle is not
  already that name — the test is the value, not the provider, so a GitHub
  account that does carry a display name grows the row like any other. In JSON
  the field is `display_name`, not `name`: `sessions[].name` in the same
  envelope is a session's name, and one document must not spell two subjects
  the same way — it also matches `entire experts` and /me's own `displayName`.
  It is uncollapsed, as `--json` never applies a text-view collapse.
  The same mapping runs in reverse wherever a grantee is typed:
  `/identity/handles` resolves only the stored `google-<subject id>`, so
  `entire grant` restores the prefix before resolving and accepts either
  spelling. `grant … list` tables and pickers show the display form too, so
  `user`, list rows and the accepted grantee are one spelling for every
  provider in text output. Every `--json` surface keeps the wire value instead
  — `auth status --json` `user` included (`google:google-100…`) — so a script
  can compare it with `grant … list --json` grantee names directly. `auth status` also marks the caller's
  own row `(current)`, matching the login JWT's `fid` (refresh-token family id)
  claim against the listed session ids, since a session IS a refresh-token
  family. That match is the only thing entitling the verdict line to state an
  expiry: an unmatched claim renders neither marker nor expiry rather than
  borrowing another session's, because everything reachable from here
  (`logout`, `logout --everywhere`) ends sessions. `logout` sweeps every saved
  login: one `DELETE /api/auth/tokens` per login server ends every CLI session
  there (core tells them apart by `issuer_client_id`), then the login is
  removed locally. Nothing narrows it: an explicit `--context` is refused
  (`errContextFlagOnLogout`) rather than ignored, since it reads as a request
  to end one login, and `$ENTIRE_CONTEXT` is ignored as ambient state.

  elsewhere and cannot be renewed`, with the verdict line carrying the *bearer's*
  remaining life instead of a session lifetime, since with nothing left to renew
  it that is when the user is logged out (`login_revoked` / `token_expires_at`

  endpoint includes the caller's own session — that is how a matched `fid` finds

  truncation explains zero. **With sessions listed**, absence is the only

  mint one is evidence of nothing and stays quiet. Do not gate this on the
  refresh having failed: that only becomes known when a refresh is *attempted
  and fails*, and a token still far from expiry is returned without contacting
  the server, so requiring it left the notice silent in the commonest case —
  every session revoked while the current bearer still had hours to run. Zero sessions still reports, being a contradiction worth seeing.

  session at once, browser logins included, and in the collapsed view those

  never sized by a number: `logout` sweeps every saved login on every login
  server, while the rows on screen are one server's, so a count there would
  understate what the command destroys. The whole logout hint is
  withheld once a login is known revoked — any session still listed belongs to
  the login that replaced this one, so there is nothing here worth ending, and
  the notice above already names `entire login` as the action.

  instant renders as a flat `expired` rather than `expires 19h ago`, which would
  contradict the "Logged in" beside it, and an unreadable one is dropped rather
  than echoed mid-sentence (the session table still shows it verbatim in a cell
  of its own, and `--json` carries it untouched). The `--sessions` table's

  heading supplies the verb, so a cell reading `19h ago` says "expired" only by
  implication, which a reader scanning the column will not pick up. `CREATED`
  and `LAST USED` keep the plain relative form, the past being the tense they
  report. Because that deadline is the

  rendered — a session whose `expires_at` is empty or unparseable keeps its

  over every stored context. Every runtime failure reachable once `--json`
  is set likewise prints an envelope carrying `error`, so `--json | jq
  .logged_in` parses: a hard fetch failure (network, DNS, 5xx), an unresolvable
  target (malformed `ENTIRE_TOKEN`, unreadable `contexts.json`, unknown
  `--context`) and the TLS refusal on an `http://` login server all route
  through one helper. A usage error is the deliberate exception: `auth status
  --json sessions` is refused by `cobra.NoArgs` before `RunE` runs, so it exits
  non-zero with empty stdout and a suggestion on stderr. The command keeps its
  non-zero exit and prints nothing further to stderr. The JSON carries the provider-qualified

  caller has to rejoin. **Identity is split across providers**, so the view takes
  whichever half each one has. GitHub supplies a human handle
  (`github:gtrrz-victor`); Google supplies a display name and a handle
  minted as `google-<subject id>`, which would qualify to `google:google-100…`
  — the provider twice. How each provider's handle is shown and typed is owned
  by `providerIdentity` (`provider_identity.go`): GitHub handles pass through
  unchanged (so a user genuinely named `github-foo` keeps that name), while
  Google's render as `google:<subject id>`. A `name` row
  carries the display name, and earns its line only where the handle is not
  already that name — the test is the value, not the provider, so a GitHub
  account that does carry a display name grows the row like any other. In JSON

  envelope is a session's name, and one document must not spell two subjects
  the same way — it also matches `entire experts` and /me's own `displayName`.
  It is uncollapsed, as `--json` never applies a text-view collapse.
  The same mapping runs in reverse wherever a grantee is typed:
  `/identity/handles` resolves only the stored `google-<subject id>`, so
  `entire grant` restores the prefix before resolving and accepts either
  spelling. `grant … list` tables and pickers show the display form too, so
  `user`, list rows and the accepted grantee are one spelling for every
  provider in text output. Every `--json` surface keeps the wire value instead
  — `auth status --json` `user` included (`google:google-100…`) — so a script
  can compare it with `grant … list --json` grantee names directly. `auth status` also marks the caller's

  expiry: an unmatched claim renders neither marker nor expiry rather than

#### Where agent-facing text goes

| What you have | Where it goes |
| --- | --- |
| A new command | `agentHelpClassification` in `agent_help_cmd.go` — one entry, keyed by command path, carrying `audience` and `listed` |
| "When to use this at all" advice for agents | `agentHelpGuidance` — **never** cobra `Short`/`Long` |
| A fact humans need too (e.g. "this output is not stable") | cobra `Long`. Human help is a reference, not a lecture: whoever typed `--help` already chose the command |
| A per-task command recommendation | `agent-help`, which is pulled on demand. The first-turn injection stays focused on the project-trail workflow below |

**Flag it; don't decide it.** Whether a command is `listed`, and whether it is
read-only / task-driven / user-owned, are product judgment calls — they change
what agents do unprompted in every user's repo. Take the safe default
(unlisted, user-owned), then say in the PR what you picked and why so a human
can move it. Never quietly promote a command into the listing or into
read-only.

CI enforces the mechanical parts, so trust these rather than re-deriving them:
every advertised top-level command and every child of a listed group is
classified; a read-only group contains no writing subcommand; guidance text
never appears in a command's `Short`/`Long`.

Hidden commands opt into being advertised here by setting
`Annotations[agentHelpAnnotation] = "true"` (e.g. `trail`). Because `agent-help`
renders live and lists non-hidden commands, the experimental commands appear in
`agent-help` in developer/nightly builds and are absent in stable releases — the
advertised surface is build-dependent, matching what `entire help` shows.
No-channel agents (Cursor, Copilot CLI, Factory Droid, MCP hosts — no
context-injection channel and no agent-help skill template) reach it without an
active push. All of them can discover it passively: it is visible in `entire
help`, the `entire status` footer points at it, and `entire status --json`
exposes it as the `agent_help` field. On top of that, Factory AI Droid (which is
banner-only) gets the pointer appended to its SessionStart hook banner, and
MCP-host agents can launch the hidden `entire mcp` stdio server, which exposes
`agent_help` and `entire_status` as MCP tools using the same live rendering.
Enabling a no-channel agent with `--agent-help-skill` reports the skill
unsupported and points the agent at this passive path instead.

Cobra-native aliases (no hint): `sessions` → `session`, `cp`/`checkpoints` →
`checkpoint`.

Hidden infrastructure commands: `hooks`, `trail`,
`curl-bash-post-install`, `__send_analytics`, `__sweep_sessions`, `mcp` (MCP
stdio server for MCP-host agents).

Diagnostic subcommands live alongside `doctor.go` as `doctor_logs.go` and
`doctor_bundle.go`. Group roots and noun-group children live in files
named `<noun>_group.go` and `<noun>_<verb>.go` respectively.

### Error Handling

The CLI uses a specific pattern for error output to avoid duplication between Cobra and main.go.

**How it works:**

- `root.go` sets `SilenceErrors: true` globally - Cobra never prints errors
- `main.go` prints errors to stderr, unless the error is a `SilentError`
- Commands return `NewSilentError(err)` when they've already printed a custom message

**When to use `SilentError`:**
Use `NewSilentError()` when you want to print a custom, user-friendly error message instead of the raw error:

```go
// In a command's RunE function:
if _, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(); err != nil {
    cmd.SilenceUsage = true  // Don't show usage for prerequisite errors
    fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Not a git repository. Please run 'entire enable' from within a git repository.")
    return NewSilentError(errors.New("not a git repository"))
}
```

**When NOT to use `SilentError`:**
For normal errors where the default error message is sufficient, return the error directly. main.go will print it:

```go
// Normal error - main.go will print "unknown strategy: foo"
return fmt.Errorf("unknown strategy: %s", name)
```

**Key files:**

- `errors.go` - Defines `SilentError` type and `NewSilentError()` constructor
- `root.go` - Sets `SilenceErrors: true` on root command
- `main.go` - Checks for `SilentError` before printing

### `entire review` Command

`entire review` runs a configured review profile. Keep documentation brief and user-facing.

See [Review Command](../architecture/review-command.md) for usage, minimal profile config, and key files.

### Agent-Safe CLI Fallbacks

When building CLI features, do not make useful output available only through a
TUI, picker, wizard, terminal selection menu, confirmation dialog, or stdin
question. Agents must be able to complete the same read-only workflow from a
non-interactive terminal.

Plain text output is acceptable when it contains the full information needed for
the workflow. JSON is preferred for structured data, following existing patterns
such as `--json` on `status`, `agent-help`, `sessions`, `search`, and trail
finding commands. Long human-readable output may use a pager in TTY mode, but
must provide a bypass like the existing `--no-pager` pattern on `explain`.

For interactive browsing flows, provide one of these non-interactive shapes:

- a list command that prints stable identifiers, plus a show/detail command that
  accepts an identifier
- a flag or positional argument that selects the item directly
- a complete text or JSON fallback when stdout is not a terminal, like existing
  static/text fallbacks for TUI-backed commands

When reviewing CLI changes, inspect terminal-gated paths such as
`IsTerminalWriter`, `CanPromptInteractively`, Bubble Tea, `huh`, direct stdin
reads, terminal selection menus, confirmation dialogs, and wizard flows. Flag
the change if a non-interactive agent can only see a menu, preview, truncated
summary, or cannot select the item whose details matter.

Tests for interactive CLI features should cover the non-interactive path. See
[Spawning subprocesses in tests](testing.md#spawning-subprocesses-in-tests-tty-detection)
for the `execx.NonInteractive` pattern when testing a real `entire` command.

Existing good patterns:

- `entire review --findings`-style listings print a complete plain-text list and
  include a `view: ...` hint naming the detail command.
- `entire repo clone /gh/...` prompts only when several clusters are possible;
  without a TTY it asks for `--cluster`.
- `entire experts --tui` is safe because the TUI is opt-in and non-TTY output
  falls back to deterministic plain text.
- `entire explain --no-pager` is the local pattern for avoiding pager-only long
  text output.
- `entire status --json`, `entire agent-help --json`, `entire sessions list --json`,
  and trail finding commands show the local `--json` convention.

Do not require JSON everywhere. Human-readable text is fine if it contains the
complete information an agent needs. The failure mode is requiring an
interactive terminal to select something or reveal details.

## Accessibility

The CLI supports an accessibility mode for users who rely on screen readers. This mode uses simpler text prompts instead of interactive TUI elements.

### Environment Variable

- `ACCESSIBLE=1` (or any non-empty value) enables accessibility mode
- Users can set this in their shell profile (`.bashrc`, `.zshrc`) for persistent use

### Implementation Guidelines

When adding new interactive forms or prompts using `huh`:

**In the `cli` package:**
Use `NewAccessibleForm()` instead of `huh.NewForm()`:

```go
// Good - respects ACCESSIBLE env var
form := NewAccessibleForm(
    huh.NewGroup(
        huh.NewSelect[string]().
            Title("Choose an option").
            Options(...).
            Value(&choice),
    ),
)

// Bad - ignores accessibility setting
form := huh.NewForm(...)
```

**Outside the `cli` package (including `strategy`):**
Use `uiform.New(...)` from `cmd/entire/cli/uiform`. It applies the standard theme
and accessibility mode centrally; `NewAccessibleForm` is the CLI wrapper around
it. Wrap confirmations and other fields in a form, and do not duplicate the
`IsAccessibleMode` / `WithAccessible` wiring at call sites.

### Key Points

- Always use the accessibility helpers for any `huh` forms/prompts
- Test new interactive features with `ACCESSIBLE=1` to ensure they work
- The accessible mode is documented in `--help` output

2026-10-21 · @Paulo Gomes

## 1. Role and operating mode

You are the lead engineer and orchestrator for `entire-rsl`, a read-only Go CLI that the Entire CLI dispatches as the external command `entire rsl`. It lets a user inspect a repository's gittuf Reference State Log (RSL) for a branch, tag or Entire checkpoint: who pushed it, when, and whether gittuf verification passes for that ref.

You work in exactly two phases:

1. **Phase 0 — questions.** Read this spec, then the referenced sources (entireio/cli and gittuf). Send the user ONE message containing every question in section 2, each with its default. Stop and wait. Do not scaffold, commit or install anything before the answers arrive.
2. **Phase 1 — autonomous build.** After the answers, build to the definition of done in section 8 without further check-ins. A reply of “defaults” accepts every default.

Rules for Phase 1:

- Ask again only for a hard blocker: a destructive action, a missing credential, or a contradiction between the answers and this spec. Everything else is a decision you make and record.
- Record each non-obvious decision in `docs/decisions.md` as a dated entry: context, decision, alternatives rejected.
- Precedence when sources disagree: the user’s Phase 0 answers, then this spec, then entireio/cli conventions (`CLAUDE.md`, `docs/development/*`, `docs/architecture/external-commands.md`), then Go community defaults.
- Never guess how `entire` or gittuf behaves. Read their source at the pinned version and cite the file in your decision log.
- You may delegate bounded tasks (tests, fixtures, docs) to sub-agents. You own integration, every commit, and every review cycle.
- Finish with a short report: what shipped, decisions taken, rejected review findings, and open follow-ups.

| 8 | Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 verification failed or unprotected. |

| 17 | Accept the gittuf dependency tree and its binary size. |
| 18 | `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT` wins over CWD discovery. Log the difference at debug level. |
| 19 | A ref with no RSL entries reports `no RSL entries` with a hint that coverage may exclude it. `verify` exits 3. |
| 20 | Reviews cover this repository only, not the gittuf fork. |

# Security Policy

We take security seriously at Entire. We appreciate your efforts to responsibly disclose vulnerabilities and will make every effort to acknowledge your contributions.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

**Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.**

Instead, please send security-related reports to **[security@entire.io](mailto:security@entire.io)**.

### What to Include

When reporting a vulnerability, please include:

1. **Description** - A clear description of the vulnerability
2. **Impact** - What an attacker could achieve by exploiting this issue
3. **Steps to reproduce** - Detailed steps to reproduce the vulnerability
4. **Affected versions** - Which versions of the CLI are affected (if known)
5. **Suggested fix** - If you have ideas on how to fix it (optional)

### What to Expect

- **Acknowledgment** - We will acknowledge receipt of your report within 48 hours
- **Updates** - We will keep you informed of our progress as we investigate
- **Resolution** - We aim to resolve critical vulnerabilities within 90 days

## Confidentiality

**All reports will be kept confidential.** We will not share your information with third parties without your consent, except as required by law.

## Supported Versions

We recommend always running the latest version of the Entire CLI.

## Scope

This security policy applies to:

- The Entire CLI (`entire` command-line tool)
- Official Entire GitHub repositories
- Entire-related services at entire.io

### Out of Scope

The following are generally not considered security vulnerabilities:

- Issues in third-party dependencies (please report these upstream)
- Social engineering attacks
- Denial of service attacks
- Issues requiring physical access to a user's device

---

## Security Advisories

Security advisories are issued when a confirmed vulnerability can be exploited by a remote or non-local actor. Because the Entire CLI is primarily used as a local development tool, the following are generally treated as **bug reports rather than security advisories**:

- Regular expression performance issues (ReDoS) that only affect local execution
- Resource exhaustion that requires local access to trigger
- Issues that cannot be exploited without direct access to the user's machine

Use [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) to report bugs.

---

Thank you for helping keep Entire and our community safe!

# Security Policy

We take security seriously at Entire. We appreciate your efforts to responsibly disclose vulnerabilities and will make every effort to acknowledge your contributions.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

**Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.**

Instead, please send security-related reports to **[security@entire.io](mailto:security@entire.io)**.

### What to Include

When reporting a vulnerability, please include:

1. **Description** - A clear description of the vulnerability
2. **Impact** - What an attacker could achieve by exploiting this issue
3. **Steps to reproduce** - Detailed steps to reproduce the vulnerability
4. **Affected versions** - Which versions of entire-rsl are affected (if known)
5. **Suggested fix** - If you have ideas on how to fix it (optional)

### What to Expect

- **Acknowledgment** - We will acknowledge receipt of your report within 48 hours
- **Updates** - We will keep you informed of our progress as we investigate
- **Resolution** - We aim to resolve critical vulnerabilities within 90 days

## Confidentiality

**All reports will be kept confidential.** We will not share your information with third parties without your consent, except as required by law.

## Supported Versions

We recommend always running the latest version of entire-rsl.

## Scope

entire-rsl reports whether a repository's gittuf Reference State Log verifies. Its output is a security statement, so the following are in scope in particular:

- Any case where entire-rsl reports `verified` for a ref whose RSL history does not pass gittuf verification, has no applicable policy, or could not be fully evaluated
- Terminal escape or control sequences from repository data reaching the terminal through text output
- Any write to refs, objects or git config other than the remote-tracking RSL refs written by a confirmed fetch
- Argument or option injection into the git subprocesses entire-rsl runs

### Out of Scope

The following are generally not considered security vulnerabilities:

- Issues in third-party dependencies, including gittuf itself (please report these upstream)
- The contents of RSL custom fields, which entire-rsl labels as asserted and never uses for a verification outcome
- Social engineering attacks
- Denial of service attacks
- Issues requiring physical access to a user's device

---

Thank you for helping keep Entire and our community safe!
EOF

cat > CLAUDE.md <<'EOF'
# entire-rsl

Read-only Go CLI that the Entire CLI dispatches as `entire rsl`. It reports,
for a branch, tag or Entire checkpoint, what the gittuf Reference State Log
(RSL) records and whether gittuf verification passes. `SPEC.md` is the build
spec. Its section 9 (Phase 0 answers) overrides the rest. Decisions with their
sources are in `docs/decisions.md`.

## Commands

| When | Run |
| --- | --- |
| Before every commit | `mise run check` (fmt, lint, `go test -race`) |
| Build | `mise run build` |
| Snapshot release | `mise run snapshot` |
| Vulnerabilities | `mise run vuln` |
| Licenses | `mise run lint:licenses` |

## Layout

- `cmd/entire-rsl/main.go`: entry point. Signals, exit code via `cli.Report`.
- `cmd/entire-rsl/cli/`: Cobra commands, one file per verb (`rsl_<verb>.go`).
- `internal/` packages: see each package's doc comment.

## Rules that are easy to break

- **Read-only.** Nothing writes refs, objects, config or the RSL. The go-git
  store returns `ErrReadOnly` from every write method, and a source-guard test
  fails on write APIs outside the `--fetch` allowlist. Do not add a write path.
- **Fail closed.** Only gittuf's verifier decides `verified`. Any error during
  verification is `error`. A ref no rule covers is `unprotected`. Custom fields
  never influence a state or an exit code.
- **Untrusted output.** Every repository-sourced string printed as text goes
  through `internal/sanitize`. JSON uses standard escaping.
- **Output streams.** Results on `cmd.OutOrStdout()`, diagnostics on
  `cmd.ErrOrStderr()`. Never `os.Stdout`/`os.Stderr` outside `main.go`.
- **Environment.** Only `ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION`, `ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT`,
  `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR`, `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL` and standard variables are read,
  through `cli.Options.Getenv`.
- **git subprocesses** go through `internal/gitcli`: absolute git path, argument
  slice, `--` before positionals, repo selectors stripped, `core.fsmonitor` and
  `core.hooksPath` neutralised.

## Tests

- `t.Parallel()` everywhere, `testify`, isolated temp repositories from
  `internal/testutil`. Never touch the developer's repo or global git config.
- Golden files live in `testdata/`. Regenerate with `go test ./... -update`
  and review the diff.
- No section comments, no comments restating the next line.

## Commits

`area: summary` messages, one logical change each, unsigned (repo-local
`commit.gpgsign=false`), ending with `Assisted-by` then `Signed-off-by`.
EOF

# entire-rsl

`entire rsl` shows what a repository's [gittuf](https://gittuf.dev) Reference
State Log (RSL) records for a branch, tag or Entire checkpoint: who pushed it,
when, and whether gittuf verification passes. It is a plugin for the
[Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) and also runs standalone as
`entire-rsl`.

entire-rsl is read-only. It never writes refs, objects or git config, except
for remote-tracking RSL refs written by a fetch you confirm.

## Install

```sh
entire plugin install ./dist/entire-rsl_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz
```

## Usage

```sh
entire rsl version
```

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
EOF

#!/bin/sh

set -e

before="$(cat go.mod go.sum | git hash-object --stdin)"
go mod tidy
after="$(cat go.mod go.sum | git hash-object --stdin)"

# Compare contents rather than git status, so staged but uncommitted module
# changes do not count as untidy.
if [ "$before" != "$after" ]; then

  go.sum.

EOF

cat > internal/testutil/testutil_test.go <<'EOF'
package testutil

import (
	"os"
	"testing"

	"github.com/gittuf/gittuf/pkg/policy"
	"github.com/gittuf/gittuf/pkg/rsl"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
	IsolateGitConfig()
	os.Exit(m.Run())
}

func TestFixtureVerifiesWithGittuf(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	r := NewRepo(t)
	r.Bootstrap()

	commit := r.Commit("refs/heads/main", "first")
	entry := r.Record(r.Cluster, "refs/heads/main", rsl.CustomFields{"custom.entire.io/pusher": "01J9ZAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA (jane)"})

	tip, err := policy.VerifyRef(t.Context(), r.Git, "refs/heads/main")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, commit, tip)

	got, err := rsl.GetEntry(r.Git, entry)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	refEntry, ok := got.(*rsl.ReferenceEntry)
	require.True(t, ok)
	value, ok := refEntry.GetCustomField("custom.entire.io/pusher")
	require.True(t, ok)
	assert.Equal(t, "01J9ZAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA (jane)", value)
}

func TestFixtureRogueSignatureFailsGittuf(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	r := NewRepo(t)
	r.Bootstrap()
	r.Commit("refs/heads/main", "first")
	r.Record(r.Rogue, "refs/heads/main", nil)

	_, err := policy.VerifyRef(t.Context(), r.Git, "refs/heads/main")
	require.Error(t, err)
}

func TestFixtureIsDeterministic(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	build := func() string {
		r := NewRepo(t)
		r.Bootstrap()
		r.Commit("refs/heads/main", "first")
		return r.Record(r.Cluster, "refs/heads/main", nil).String()
	}

	assert.Equal(t, build(), build())
}

func TestKeyFingerprintIsStable(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	a := NewKey(t, "cluster")
	b := NewKey(t, "cluster")

	assert.Equal(t, a.Fingerprint(t), b.Fingerprint(t))
	assert.NotEqual(t, a.Fingerprint(t), NewKey(t, "rogue").Fingerprint(t))
}
EOF

cat > internal/store/store_test.go <<'EOF'
package store

import (
	"errors"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/entireio/entire-rsl/internal/testutil"
	"github.com/gittuf/gittuf/pkg/githash"
	"github.com/gittuf/gittuf/pkg/gitinterface"
	"github.com/gittuf/gittuf/pkg/gitstore"
	"github.com/gittuf/gittuf/pkg/policy"
	"github.com/gittuf/gittuf/pkg/rsl"
	gogit "github.com/go-git/go-git/v6"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
	testutil.IsolateGitConfig()
	os.Exit(m.Run())
}

func open(t *testing.T, dir string) *Store {
	t.Helper()

	repo, err := gogit.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	s, err := New(repo)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	return s
}

// rslEntryIDs walks the RSL from its tip and returns every entry ID.
func rslEntryIDs(t *testing.T, s gitstore.Storer) []githash.Hash {
	t.Helper()

	entry, err := rsl.GetLatestEntry(s)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var ids []githash.Hash
	for {
		ids = append(ids, entry.GetID())
		entry, err = rsl.GetParentForEntry(s, entry)
		if errors.Is(err, rsl.ErrRSLEntryNotFound) {
			return ids
		}
		require.NoError(t, err)
	}
}

// requireSame asserts that both stores return the same value and error
// presence for one call.
func requireSame[T any](t *testing.T, call string, want T, wantErr error, got T, gotErr error) {
	t.Helper()

	if wantErr != nil {
		assert.Error(t, gotErr, call)
		return
	}
	require.NoError(t, gotErr, call)
	assert.Equal(t, want, got, call)
}

func TestMatchesGitinterfaceOnScenario(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	ref := sc.Git
	got := open(t, sc.Dir)

	ids := rslEntryIDs(t, ref)
	require.NotEmpty(t, ids)

	var commits []githash.Hash
	for _, id := range ids {
		commits = append(commits, id)

		wantMsg, wantErr := ref.GetCommitMessage(id)
		gotMsg, gotErr := got.GetCommitMessage(id)
		requireSame(t, "GetCommitMessage "+id.String(), wantMsg, wantErr, gotMsg, gotErr)

		wantTree, wantErr := ref.GetCommitTreeID(id)
		gotTree, gotErr := got.GetCommitTreeID(id)
		requireSame(t, "GetCommitTreeID", wantTree, wantErr, gotTree, gotErr)

		wantParents, wantErr := ref.GetCommitParentIDs(id)
		gotParents, gotErr := got.GetCommitParentIDs(id)
		requireSame(t, "GetCommitParentIDs", wantParents, wantErr, gotParents, gotErr)

		wantPayload, wantSig, wantErr := ref.GetObjectSignature(id)
		gotPayload, gotSig, gotErr := got.GetObjectSignature(id)
		requireSame(t, "GetObjectSignature payload", wantPayload, wantErr, gotPayload, gotErr)
		requireSame(t, "GetObjectSignature signature", wantSig, wantErr, gotSig, gotErr)
	}

	refs := []string{"refs/heads/main", "refs/heads/feature", "refs/heads/rogue", "refs/heads/fixed", "refs/tags/v1.0.0", rsl.Ref, policy.Ref, policy.StagingRef, testutil.CheckpointRef(testutil.CheckpointULID), "refs/heads/missing", "HEAD"}
	for _, name := range refs {
		wantTip, wantErr := ref.GetReference(name)
		gotTip, gotErr := got.GetReference(name)
		requireSame(t, "GetReference "+name, wantTip, wantErr, gotTip, gotErr)
		if errors.Is(wantErr, gitstore.ErrReferenceNotFound) {
			assert.ErrorIs(t, gotErr, gitstore.ErrReferenceNotFound, name)
		}
		if wantErr == nil {
			commits = append(commits, wantTip)

// rslEntryIDs walks the RSL from its tip and returns every entry ID.
func rslEntryIDs(t *testing.T, s gitstore.Storer) []githash.Hash {
	t.Helper()

	entry, err := rsl.GetLatestEntry(s)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var ids []githash.Hash
	for {
		ids = append(ids, entry.GetID())
		entry, err = rsl.GetParentForEntry(s, entry)
		if errors.Is(err, rsl.ErrRSLEntryNotFound) {
			return ids
		}
		require.NoError(t, err)
	}
}

	t.Helper()

	if wantErr != nil {
		assert.Error(t, gotErr, call)
		return
	}
	require.NoError(t, gotErr, call)
	assert.Equal(t, want, got, call)
}

cat >> docs/decisions.md <<'EOF'

## 2026-10-21: A read-only go-git store of our own

- **Context:** Phase 0 asks for a go-git backed store. gittuf's own go-git
  backend (`internal/gogitstore`) is internal, delegates several reads to the
  git binary, and is reachable only in developer mode
  (`experimental/gittuf/storer.go:83`).
- **Decision:** `internal/store` implements `gitstore.Storer` over go-git
  entirely in-process. Object reads follow `internal/gogitstore`, and the
  remaining reads (`GetCommitsBetweenRange`, `GetFilePathsChangedByCommit`,
  `KnowsCommit`, `LookupConfig`) mirror `pkg/gitinterface` (`log.go:14`,
  `changes.go:17`, `commit.go:239`, `config.go:20`). Every write method,
  including `GetMergeTree`, returns `ErrReadOnly`, which makes the read-only
  guarantee structural for anything gittuf does through the store.
  `GetMergeTree` is only used by `VerifyMergeable`
  (`internal/policy/verify.go:210`), never by `VerifyRef`.
- **Verification:** differential tests run every read, plus `VerifyRef` and
  `VerifyRefFromEntry`, against `gitinterface.Repository` on the fixture
  repositories and require identical results.
- **Hardening:** objects are size-checked before decoding (1 MiB commits and
  tags, 16 MiB trees and blobs). `GetReference` accepts only `HEAD` and full
  `refs/` names. gitinterface would pass revision expressions to `rev-parse`.
  `LookupConfig` reads the repository's own config only.
- **Rejected:** `gitinterface.Repository` (shells out to git for every read)
  and enabling gittuf's backend through developer mode.

## 2026-10-21: Fixtures isolate git config in TestMain

- **Context:** fixtures are written by gittuf's git binary backed store, which
  inherits the process environment, so a developer's `commit.gpgsign` or other
  global config would change fixture commits.
- **Decision:** test binaries that build fixtures call
  `testutil.IsolateGitConfig` from `TestMain`, setting `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` to
  the null device and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` before any test runs. Tests stay
  parallel because nothing changes the environment afterwards.
- **Rejected:** `t.Setenv`, which forbids `t.Parallel()`.
EOF

## 4. How a repo's root of trust is created

**Who holds the root key.** A single fleet root, kept on the server (`custody: server_held`, threshold 1; clusters.prod.yaml:9-23). Its seed is stored encrypted with KMS in Secrets Manager. It is fetched per generation by `core/trust/rootseed_provider.go:12-20` and unwrapped inside entire-core. `core/trust/author.go:62-89` checks it against the reviewed profile key before signing anything.

**What gets authorized.** `core/trust/policyrequest.go:92-149` (`AuthorPolicyRequest`) includes every `pending` and `active` signer from every cluster the repo is placed on (primary plus native mirrors), and leaves out `retiring` signers. It fails if any placement has no authorized signer.

**Building the signed policy.** `core/trust/author.go:101-131` builds a `gittufstore.AuthorPolicyInput`. For a first bootstrap it calls `gittufstore.AuthorBootstrapClosure`, which creates a policy commit with no parent; later changes use `AuthorSuccessorClosure`. `gittufstore/closure.go:160-168` then calls the fork's `policy.Author` (in place of `policy.Bootstrap`):
```go
treeID, err := policy.Author(ctx, store, policy.BootstrapParams{
    RootSigners:         []crypto.Signer{rootPriv},
    RootPublicKeys:      cryptoPublicKeys(in.RootPublicKeys),
    RootThreshold:       in.RootThreshold,
    RSLSignerPublicKeys: cryptoPublicKeys(in.RSLSignerPublicKeys),
    RefPatterns:         in.RefPatterns,
    ...
```

**Inside the fork** (`pkg/policy/policy.go`):
- The root keys go into both the root role and the primary rule file, with the root threshold (lines 641-664).
- The RSL signers are added as principals in a single targets rule: `const rslSignerRuleName = "authorize-rsl-signers"` (line 63), created with `targetsMetadata.AddRule(rslSignerRuleName, ids, p.RefPatterns, p.rslSignerThreshold())` (line 682). The RSL signer threshold defaults to 1 (lines 456-462).

**RefPatterns: `git:refs/*`.** Set at `/home/coder/git/entirehq/entiredb/internal/entirecore/trust_reconciler.go:58`:
```go
func trustReconcilerRefPatterns() []string { return []string{"git:refs/*"} }
```
The comment at lines 43-57 says this is intentionally the all-refs wildcard rather than the narrower set the ADR targets ("refs/gittuf/policy + refs/entire/checkpoints/* + refs/tags/* + default branch"). Narrowing is tracked in ENT-1605. The value is passed in at line 541 through `nativemirror.TrustReconcilerConfig.RefPatterns`.

**Expiry.** Defaults to 10 years (`core/nativemirror/trust_reconciler.go:236`).

**Publication.** `rslstore/publish.go` `PublishPolicy` (line 103) does a compare-and-swap on `refs/gittuf/policy`. On bootstrap, `recordBaseline` (lines 264-330) throws away any RSL entries written before the policy and starts the baseline at entry 1. Those baseline entries carry the `entire-trust-service` actor.

**Per-repo state.** Lifecycle states are `disabled` → `bootstrap_pending` → `rooted` (`rslstore/writer.go` `LifecycleFunc` comment). func TestOpenWithoutRSL(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	r := testutil.NewRepo(t)
	r.Commit("refs/heads/main", "only")

	_, err := Open(openStore(t, r.Dir))

	require.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrNoRSL)
}

func TestLogNewestFirstWithAnnotations(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	r := openReader(t, sc.Dir)

	entries, err := r.Log(t.Context(), LogOptions{Limit: 100})
	require.NoError(t, err)

	require.Equal(t, sc.FixedEntry, entries[0].ID)
	assert.Equal(t, r.Tip(), entries[0].ID)
	for i := 1; i < len(entries); i++ {
		assert.Greater(t, entries[i-1].Number, entries[i].Number, "numbers decrease")
	}

	byID := map[string]Entry{}
	for _, e := range entries {
		byID[e.ID.String()] = e
	}

	annot := byID[sc.RevokeAnnot.String()]
	assert.Equal(t, KindAnnotation, annot.Kind)
	assert.True(t, annot.Skip)
	assert.Equal(t, "revoked: signed by an unknown key", annot.Message)
	assert.Equal(t, []githash.Hash{sc.RevokedEntry}, annot.Annotates)

	revoked := byID[sc.RevokedEntry.String()]
	assert.True(t, revoked.Skipped())
	assert.Equal(t, []githash.Hash{sc.RevokeAnnot}, revoked.SkippedBy)

	main := byID[sc.MainLastEntry.String()]
	assert.Equal(t, KindReference, main.Kind)
	assert.Equal(t, "refs/heads/main", main.RefName)
	assert.Equal(t, sc.TrailerCommit, main.TargetID)
	assert.Equal(t, testutil.PusherJane, main.CustomFields["custom.entire.io/pusher"])
	assert.False(t, main.Time.IsZero())
	assert.Equal(t, "Jane Doe", main.Committer.Name)
}

func TestSignatureAttribution(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	r := openReader(t, sc.Dir)

	entries, err := r.Log(t.Context(), LogOptions{Limit: 100})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	byID := map[string]Entry{}
	for _, e := range entries {
		byID[e.ID.String()] = e
	}

	cluster := byID[sc.MainLastEntry.String()].Signature
	assert.Equal(t, Signature{Method: MethodSSH, KeyID: sc.Cluster.Fingerprint(t), Valid: true}, cluster)

	rogue := byID[sc.RogueEntry.String()].Signature
	assert.Equal(t, Signature{Method: MethodSSH, KeyID: sc.Rogue.Fingerprint(t), Valid: true}, rogue)

	policyEntry := entries[len(entries)-1].Signature
	assert.Equal(t, MethodNone, policyEntry.Method)
	assert.False(t, policyEntry.Valid)
	assert.Empty(t, policyEntry.KeyID)
}

func TestTamperedPayloadIsNotAttributed(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	payload, sig, err := sc.Git.GetObjectSignature(sc.MainLastEntry)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	got := checkSignature(append(payload, []byte("tampered")...), sig)

	assert.Equal(t, MethodSSH, got.Method)
	assert.False(t, got.Valid)
	assert.Empty(t, got.KeyID, "an unverified signature must not name a key")
	assert.NotEmpty(t, got.Problem)
}

func TestCheckSignatureFormats(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name string
		sig  string
		want string
	}{
		{name: "none", sig: "", want: MethodNone},
		{name: "gpg", sig: "-----BEGIN PGP SIGNATURE-----\nabc\n-----END PGP SIGNATURE-----\n", want: MethodGPG},
		{name: "x509", sig: "-----BEGIN SIGNED MESSAGE-----\nabc\n-----END SIGNED MESSAGE-----\n", want: MethodX509},
		{name: "garbage", sig: "hello", want: MethodUnknown},
		{name: "malformed ssh", sig: "-----BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----\nnotbase64\n-----END SSH SIGNATURE-----\n", want: MethodSSH},
		{name: "two blocks", sig: "-----BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----\na\n-----END SSH SIGNATURE-----\n-----BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----\nb\n-----END SSH SIGNATURE-----\n", want: MethodUnknown},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			got := checkSignature([]byte("payload"), []byte(tt.sig))

			assert.Equal(t, tt.want, got.Method)
			assert.False(t, got.Valid)
			assert.Empty(t, got.KeyID)
		})
	}
}

func TestLogFilters(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	r := openReader(t, sc.Dir)

	main, err := r.Log(t.Context(), LogOptions{Ref: "refs/heads/main", Limit: 100})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, main, 3)
	assert.Equal(t, sc.MainLastEntry, main[0].ID)
	assert.Equal(t, sc.MainFirstEntry, main[2].ID)

	limited, err := r.Log(t.Context(), LogOptions{Limit: 2})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, []githash.Hash{sc.FixedEntry, sc.RevokeAnnot}, ids(limited))

	before, err := ParseSelector(sc.RevokeAnnot.String())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	below, err := r.Log(t.Context(), LogOptions{Before: &before, Limit: 1})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, []githash.Hash{sc.RevokedEntry}, ids(below))

	missing, err := ParseSelector("ffffffffff")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = r.Log(t.Context(), LogOptions{Before: &missing, Limit: 1})
	require.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrEntryNotFound)
}

func TestFind(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	r := openReader(t, sc.Dir)

	byID, err := ParseSelector(sc.CheckpointEntry.String())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	e, err := r.Find(t.Context(), byID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, testutil.CheckpointRef(testutil.CheckpointULID), e.RefName)

	byPrefix, err := ParseSelector(sc.CheckpointEntry.String()[:10])
	require.NoError(t, err)
	e, err = r.Find(t.Context(), byPrefix)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, sc.CheckpointEntry, e.ID)

	byNumber, err := ParseSelector("1")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	first, err := r.Find(t.Context(), byNumber)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, uint64(1), first.Number)

	unknown, err := ParseSelector("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = r.Find(t.Context(), unknown)
	require.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrEntryNotFound)
}

func TestFindRefusesCommitsOutsideTheRSL(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	r := openReader(t, sc.Dir)

	// MainFirst is a real commit, but not an RSL entry.
	sel, err := ParseSelector(sc.MainFirst.String())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = r.Find(t.Context(), sel)

	require.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrEntryNotFound)
}

func TestHistory(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	r := openReader(t, sc.Dir)

	tag, err := r.History(t.Context(), "refs/tags/v1.0.0", 10)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, tag.Total)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, tag.Unskipped)
	assert.Equal(t, []githash.Hash{sc.TagMovedEntry, sc.TagFirstEntry}, ids(tag.Entries))

	fixed, err := r.History(t.Context(), "refs/heads/fixed", 1)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, fixed.Total)
	assert.Equal(t, 1, fixed.Unskipped)
	assert.Equal(t, []githash.Hash{sc.FixedEntry}, ids(fixed.Entries))

	none, err := r.History(t.Context(), "refs/heads/never", 10)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Zero(t, none.Total)
	assert.Empty(t, none.Entries)
}

func TestWalkStopsOnCancelledContext(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	r := openReader(t, sc.Dir)

	ctx, cancel := t.Context(), func() {}
	_ = cancel
	cctx, stop := contextWithCancel(ctx)
	stop()

	_, err := r.Log(cctx, LogOptions{Limit: 100})
	require.ErrorIs(t, err, errCanceled())
}

func TestParseSelector(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, bad := range []string{"", "0", "abc", "abcdef", "xyz1234567", "-1234567", "18446744073709551616", "a" + string(make([]byte, 70))} {
		_, err := ParseSelector(bad)
		require.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrInvalidEntryID, bad)
	}

	sel, err := ParseSelector("42")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "#42", sel.String())

	sel, err = ParseSelector("ABCDEF0")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "abcdef0", sel.String())
}

func FuzzParseSelector(f *testing.F) {
	for _, seed := range []string{"1", "42", "abcdef0", "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567", "", "-x", "#1"} {
		f.Add(seed)
	}
	f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, in string) {
		sel, err := ParseSelector(in)
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		if sel.byNumber {
			assert.NotZero(t, sel.number)
			return
		}
		assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(sel.idPrefix), minPrefix)
		assert.True(t, isHex(sel.idPrefix))
	})
}

		assert.Greater(t, entries[i-1].Number, entries[i].Number, "numbers decrease")
	}

	byID := map[string]Entry{}
	for _, e := range entries {
		byID[e.ID.String()] = e
	}

	annot := byID[sc.RevokeAnnot.String()]
	assert.Equal(t, KindAnnotation, annot.Kind)
	assert.True(t, annot.Skip)
	assert.Equal(t, "revoked: signed by an unknown key", annot.Message)
	assert.Equal(t, []githash.Hash{sc.RevokedEntry}, annot.Annotates)

	revoked := byID[sc.RevokedEntry.String()]
	assert.True(t, revoked.Skipped())
	assert.Equal(t, []githash.Hash{sc.RevokeAnnot}, revoked.SkippedBy)

	main := byID[sc.MainLastEntry.String()]
	assert.Equal(t, KindReference, main.Kind)
	assert.Equal(t, "refs/heads/main", main.RefName)
	assert.Equal(t, sc.TrailerCommit, main.TargetID)
	assert.Equal(t, testutil.PusherJane, main.CustomFields["custom.entire.io/pusher"])
	assert.False(t, main.Time.IsZero())
	assert.Equal(t, "Jane Doe", main.Committer.Name)
}

func TestSignatureAttribution(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	r := openReader(t, sc.Dir)

	entries, err := r.Log(t.Context(), LogOptions{Limit: 100})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	byID := map[string]Entry{}
	for _, e := range entries {
		byID[e.ID.String()] = e
	}

	cluster := byID[sc.MainLastEntry.String()].Signature
	assert.Equal(t, Signature{Method: MethodSSH, KeyID: sc.Cluster.Fingerprint(t), Valid: true}, cluster)

	rogue := byID[sc.RogueEntry.String()].Signature
	assert.Equal(t, Signature{Method: MethodSSH, KeyID: sc.Rogue.Fingerprint(t), Valid: true}, rogue)

	policyEntry := entries[len(entries)-1].Signature
	assert.Equal(t, MethodNone, policyEntry.Method)
	assert.False(t, policyEntry.Valid)
	assert.Empty(t, policyEntry.KeyID)
}

func TestTamperedPayloadIsNotAttributed(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	payload, sig, err := sc.Git.GetObjectSignature(sc.MainLastEntry)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	got := checkSignature(append(payload, []byte("tampered")...), sig)

	assert.Equal(t, MethodSSH, got.Method)
	assert.False(t, got.Valid)
	assert.Empty(t, got.KeyID, "an unverified signature must not name a key")
	assert.NotEmpty(t, got.Problem)
}

func TestCheckSignatureFormats(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name string
		sig  string
		want string
	}{
		{name: "none", sig: "", want: MethodNone},
		{name: "gpg", sig: "-----BEGIN PGP SIGNATURE-----\nabc\n-----END PGP SIGNATURE-----\n", want: MethodGPG},
		{name: "x509", sig: "-----BEGIN SIGNED MESSAGE-----\nabc\n-----END SIGNED MESSAGE-----\n", want: MethodX509},
		{name: "garbage", sig: "hello", want: MethodUnknown},
		{name: "malformed ssh", sig: "-----BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----\nnotbase64\n-----END SSH SIGNATURE-----\n", want: MethodSSH},
		{name: "two blocks", sig: "-----BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----\na\n-----END SSH SIGNATURE-----\n-----BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE-----\nb\n-----END SSH SIGNATURE-----\n", want: MethodUnknown},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			got := checkSignature([]byte("payload"), []byte(tt.sig))

			assert.Equal(t, tt.want, got.Method)
			assert.False(t, got.Valid)
			assert.Empty(t, got.KeyID)
		})
	}
}

func TestLogFilters(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	r := openReader(t, sc.Dir)

	main, err := r.Log(t.Context(), LogOptions{Ref: "refs/heads/main", Limit: 100})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, main, 3)
	assert.Equal(t, sc.MainLastEntry, main[0].ID)
	assert.Equal(t, sc.MainFirstEntry, main[2].ID)

	limited, err := r.Log(t.Context(), LogOptions{Limit: 2})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, []githash.Hash{sc.FixedEntry, sc.RevokeAnnot}, ids(limited))

	before, err := ParseSelector(sc.RevokeAnnot.String())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	below, err := r.Log(t.Context(), LogOptions{Before: &before, Limit: 1})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, []githash.Hash{sc.RevokedEntry}, ids(below))

	missing, err := ParseSelector("ffffffffff")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = r.Log(t.Context(), LogOptions{Before: &missing, Limit: 1})
	require.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrEntryNotFound)
}

func TestFind(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	r := openReader(t, sc.Dir)

	byID, err := ParseSelector(sc.CheckpointEntry.String())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	e, err := r.Find(t.Context(), byID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, testutil.CheckpointRef(testutil.CheckpointULID), e.RefName)

	byPrefix, err := ParseSelector(sc.CheckpointEntry.String()[:10])
	require.NoError(t, err)
	e, err = r.Find(t.Context(), byPrefix)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, sc.CheckpointEntry, e.ID)

	byNumber, err := ParseSelector("1")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	first, err := r.Find(t.Context(), byNumber)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, uint64(1), first.Number)

	unknown, err := ParseSelector("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = r.Find(t.Context(), unknown)
	require.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrEntryNotFound)
}

	t.Parallel()

	sel, err := ParseSelector(sc.MainFirst.String())

func TestHistory(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	r := openReader(t, sc.Dir)

	tag, err := r.History(t.Context(), "refs/tags/v1.0.0", 10)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, tag.Total)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, tag.Unskipped)
	assert.Equal(t, []githash.Hash{sc.TagMovedEntry, sc.TagFirstEntry}, ids(tag.Entries))

	assert.Equal(t, 2, fixed.Total)

	assert.Empty(t, none.Entries)
}

func TestWalkStopsOnCancelledContext(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	sc := testutil.NewScenario(t)
	r := openReader(t, sc.Dir)

	ctx, cancel := t.Context(), func() {}
	_ = cancel
	cctx, stop := contextWithCancel(ctx)
	stop()

	_, err := r.Log(cctx, LogOptions{Limit: 100})
	require.ErrorIs(t, err, errCanceled())
}

func TestParseSelector(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	for _, bad := range []string{"", "0", "abc", "abcdef", "xyz1234567", "-1234567", "18446744073709551616", "a" + string(make([]byte, 70))} {
		_, err := ParseSelector(bad)
		require.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrInvalidEntryID, bad)
	}

	sel, err := ParseSelector("42")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "#42", sel.String())

	sel, err = ParseSelector("ABCDEF0")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "abcdef0", sel.String())
}

func FuzzParseSelector(f *testing.F) {
	for _, seed := range []string{"1", "42", "abcdef0", "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567", "", "-x", "#1"} {
		f.Add(seed)
	}
	f.Fuzz(func(t *testing.T, in string) {
		sel, err := ParseSelector(in)
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		if sel.byNumber {
			assert.NotZero(t, sel.number)
			return
		}
		assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(sel.idPrefix), minPrefix)
		assert.True(t, isHex(sel.idPrefix))
	})
}

cat > cmd/entire-rsl/cli/sanitize_test.go <<'EOF'
package cli

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/entireio/entire-rsl/internal/testutil"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// hostile carries an OSC title change, a screen clear, a colour and a
// right-to-left override.
var hostile = "\x1b]0;pwned\x07\x1b[2J\x1b[31m" + string(rune(0x202e)) + "txt.exe"

func TestHostileRepositoryStringsRenderInert(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	r := testutil.NewRepo(t)
	r.Bootstrap()
	target := r.Commit("refs/heads/main", "only")
	evil := r.RecordAt(r.Cluster, "refs/heads/evil"+hostile, target, nil)
	annot := r.Annotate(r.Cluster, false, "note"+hostile+"\r\nsecond line", evil)

	for _, args := range [][]string{
		{"log"},
		{"entry", evil.String()},
		{"entry", annot.String()},
	} {
		res := execute(t, inRepo(r.Dir), args...)
		require.Equal(t, ExitOK, res.code, res.stderr)

		assert.NotContains(t, res.stdout, "\x1b", args)
		assert.NotContains(t, res.stdout, "\x07", args)
		assert.NotContains(t, res.stdout, "\r", args)
		assert.NotContains(t, res.stdout, string(rune(0x202e)), args)
		assert.Contains(t, res.stdout, "txt.exe", args)
	}

	res := execute(t, inRepo(r.Dir), "entry", annot.String())
	assert.Contains(t, res.stdout, "second line")

	res = execute(t, inRepo(r.Dir), "entry", "--json", evil.String())
	require.Equal(t, ExitOK, res.code)
	assert.NotContains(t, res.stdout, "\x1b", "JSON escapes control characters")
	assert.True(t, strings.Contains(res.stdout, `\u001b`), "the raw value survives in JSON, escaped")
}
EOF
mise exec -- go test -race -count=1 -run Hostile ./cmd/entire-rsl/cli/ 2>&1 | tail -20

cat > docs/json-schema.md <<'EOF'
# JSON output schema

Every command that takes `--json` prints one JSON document on stdout. Every
document carries `"schema_version": 1`. The version changes only on an
incompatible change: removing or renaming a field, or changing its type or
meaning. New fields may appear in any version, so consumers must ignore
fields they do not know.

Golden files under `cmd/entire-rsl/cli/testdata/*.json` pin every document
shape.

Conventions:

- Object IDs are full lowercase hex strings (40 characters for SHA-1, 64 for
  SHA-256).
- Times are RFC 3339 in UTC. An entry's `time` is its commit time, which the
  signer asserts. Nothing else vouches for it.
- Strings carry repository data verbatim, with standard JSON escaping.
  Control characters are escaped as `\u00XX`, but other characters, such as
  Unicode bidirectional overrides, are not. Sanitize before printing them to a
  terminal.
- Fields ending in `_unverified`, `custom_fields` and `entire` are recorded in
  the entry but not verified by entire-rsl. Never base a security decision on
  them.

## Entry

Used by `log` and `entry`.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | integer | Entry number, increasing with each entry. 0 for unnumbered entries. |
| `id` | string | Entry ID (the RSL commit). |
| `type` | string | `reference`, `annotation` or `propagation`. |
| `ref` | string | Ref the entry records. Absent for annotations. |
| `target` | string | Object the ref was set to. Absent for annotations. |
| `time` | string | Commit time, asserted by the signer. |
| `signer` | object | See [Signer](#signer). |
| `committer_unverified` | object | `name` and `email` from the commit. Not verified. |
| `skipped` | boolean | True when a skip annotation revokes this entry. |
| `skipped_by` | array of string | IDs of the skip annotations revoking this entry. |
| `annotated_by` | array of string | IDs of every annotation referring to this entry, newest first. |
| `skip` | boolean | Annotations only: whether the annotation revokes the entries it names. |
| `annotates` | array of string | Annotations only: IDs of the entries it refers to. |
| `message` | string | Annotations only: the annotation message. |
| `upstream_repository` | string | Propagation entries only. |
| `upstream_entry_id` | string | Propagation entries only. |
| `entire` | object | Entire's interpretation of `custom_fields`. See [Entire fields](#entire-fields). |
| `custom_fields` | object | Every custom field, key to value, as recorded. |

## Signer

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | string | `ssh`, `gpg`, `x509`, `none` (unsigned) or `unknown`. |
| `signature_valid` | boolean | True when entire-rsl checked the signature against the key it names. Only SSH signatures are checked. |
| `key_id` | string | SSH SHA256 fingerprint of the signing key. Present only when `signature_valid` is true. |
| `name` | string | Entire cluster that owns the key, when known. Best effort. |
| `problem` | string | Why the signature names no key. |

A valid signature proves who signed the entry, not that they were allowed
to. Only verification decides that.

## Entire fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pusher` | object | The end user Entire observed pushing: `account_id`, `handle` and `raw`. `account_id` and `handle` are absent when `raw` does not have the `<account ULID> (<handle>)` shape. |
| `actor` | string | The non-human service that performed the write, such as `entire-mirror-service`. |
| `actor_label` | string | What `actor` means, for known actors. |
| `repository` | string | Entire repository ID. |
| `force_push` | boolean | True for non-fast-forward branch updates and any tag update. |
| `operation` | string | `default-branch-change` or `default-branch-baseline`. Absent for an ordinary push. |
| `operation_label` | string | What `operation` means. |
| `symref_target` | string | For a default branch change, the new default branch. |
| `symref_previous_target` | string | For a default branch change, the previous default branch. |

## `version`

```json
{"schema_version": 1, "version": "...", "commit": "...", "go_version": "...", "gittuf_version": "..."}
```

## `log`

```json
{"schema_version": 1, "entries": [Entry, ...]}
```

Entries are newest first. `entries` is an empty array when nothing matches.

## `entry`

```json
{"schema_version": 1, "entry": Entry}
```
EOF

| `message` | string | Annotations only: the annotation message. |
| `upstream_repository` | string | Propagation entries only. |
| `upstream_entry_id` | string | Propagation entries only. |
| `entire` | object | Entire's interpretation of `custom_fields`. See [Entire fields](#entire-fields). |
| `custom_fields` | object | Every custom field, key to value, as recorded. |

## Signer

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | string | `ssh`, `gpg`, `x509`, `none` (unsigned) or `unknown`. |
| `signature_valid` | boolean | True when entire-rsl checked the signature against the key it names. Only SSH signatures are checked. |
| `key_id` | string | SSH SHA256 fingerprint of the signing key. Present only when `signature_valid` is true. |
| `name` | string | Entire cluster that owns the key, when known. Best effort. |
| `problem` | string | Why the signature names no key. |

A valid signature proves who signed the entry, not that they were allowed
to. Only verification decides that.

## Entire fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pusher` | object | The end user Entire observed pushing: `account_id`, `handle` and `raw`. `account_id` and `handle` are absent when `raw` does not have the `<account ULID> (<handle>)` shape. |
| `actor` | string | The non-human service that performed the write, such as `entire-mirror-service`. |
| `actor_label` | string | What `actor` means, for known actors. |
| `repository` | string | Entire repository ID. |
| `force_push` | boolean | True for non-fast-forward branch updates and any tag update. |
| `operation` | string | `default-branch-change` or `default-branch-baseline`. Absent for an ordinary push. |
| `operation_label` | string | What `operation` means. |
| `symref_target` | string | For a default branch change, the new default branch. |
| `symref_previous_target` | string | For a default branch change, the previous default branch. |

## `version`

```json
{"schema_version": 1, "version": "...", "commit": "...", "go_version": "...", "gittuf_version": "..."}
```

## `log`

```json
{"schema_version": 1, "entries": [Entry, ...]}
```

Entries are newest first. `entries` is an empty array when nothing matches.

## `entry`

```json
{"schema_version": 1, "entry": Entry}
```
EOF

git reset -q cmd docs && git add docs/decisions.md 2>/dev/null; cat >> docs/decisions.md <<'EOF'

## 2026-10-21: entire-rsl checks SSH signatures before naming a signer

- **Context:** the key embedded in an SSH signature is chosen by whoever made
  the signature, so naming it unchecked would let a forged entry display as
  signed by an Entire cluster in `log` and `entry`.
- **Decision:** `internal/rslread` names a key only after `sshsig.Verify`
  over the entry's signed payload, with namespace `git` and SHA-512, exactly as
  gittuf's SSH verifier does (`internal/signerverifier/ssh/ssh.go:38`).
  Signatures with more than one armored block are refused, as
  `pkg/gitinterface/signature.go` requires of verifiers. GPG and x509
  signatures are reported by method only. A valid signature proves who signed,
  not that they may: authorization stays with gittuf verification.
- **Rejected:** showing the embedded key unchecked, and reimplementing
  gittuf's policy evaluation to decide authorization in `log`.

## 2026-10-21: Cluster names come from a built-in table

- **Context:** Phase 0 answer 2 asks for the cluster name next to the signer,
  best effort and built into the CLI. Entire publishes no unauthenticated
  endpoint for signer keys.
- **Decision:** `internal/clusters` maps the public RSL signer and fleet root
  fingerprints in entiredb `core/cluster/fixtures/clusters.{prod,staging}.yaml`
  (e64a4f389a) to cluster names. A test derives each fingerprint from the
  fixture's public key. The table only labels keys and never affects trust.
- **Rejected:** fetching keys at run time, which needs network access and an
  authenticated admin route (`GET /api/admin/repos/{repoID}/trust`).

## 2026-10-21: RSL walks start at the tip and build entries lazily

- **Context:** an annotation is newer than the entries it refers to, and gittuf
  parses any commit that reads as an entry, reachable or not.
- **Decision:** every walk starts at the RSL tip, so an entry is only read when
  reachable and all its annotations have been seen first. `entry <id>` walks to
  the entry rather than parsing the named commit directly. Walks parse each
  entry, and only entries a command returns are completed with commit
  metadata and a signature check. Walks stop on context cancellation and after
  five million entries.
- **Rejected:** `rsl.GetEntry` on the named ID, which would accept commits that
  are not in the log.
EOF
git add docs/decisions.md && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
rslread: walk the RSL with annotations and checked signers

internal/rslread walks the RSL newest first from its tip, attaching every
annotation and skip to the entries it names, and selects entries by number
or ID prefix. Walks parse each entry cheaply and complete only the entries
a caller keeps, and stop on cancellation or after five million entries.

An entry names a signing key only after its SSH signature checks out with
gittuf's own parameters. Unsigned, GPG, x509 and malformed signatures are
reported without a key.

Supporting packages: sanitize strips escape sequences, control and bidi
characters from repository strings for text output. refname applies git
check-ref-format rules and refuses a leading '-'. clusters labels the
Entire cluster keys, taken from entiredb's cluster fixtures. entirefields
interprets the pusher, actor, force-push and operation fields Entire's
server stamps.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
cli: log and entry commands

log lists RSL entries newest first with their number, ID, type, ref,
target, asserted time, signer and skip status, filtered by --ref, bounded
by --limit and positioned by --before. entry shows one entry in full: its
annotations, the signer with the Entire cluster that owns the key, the
unverified committer, and Entire's custom fields labelled as asserted by
the signer.

Text output sanitizes every repository string. JSON output carries
schema_version 1, documented in docs/json-schema.md and pinned by golden
files.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Paulo Gomes <paulo@entire.io>
EOF

cd /home/coder/git/entireio/entire-gittuf && cat >> docs/json-schema.md <<'EOF'

## `branch` and `tag`

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "ref": "refs/heads/main",
  "local_tip": "...",
  "rsl_tip": "...",
  "current_entry": Entry,
  "history": [Entry, ...],
  "history_total": 3,
  "warnings": [{"code": "...", "message": "..."}]
}
```

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` | string | Full ref name. |
| `local_tip` | string or null | Local value of the ref. Null when the ref does not exist locally. |
| `rsl_tip` | string or null | Target of `current_entry`. Null when the RSL has no unskipped entry for the ref. |
| `current_entry` | Entry or null | Newest entry for the ref that no annotation skips. |
| `history` | array of Entry | Newest entries for the ref, newest first, up to `--history`, skipped ones included. |
| `history_total` | integer | Number of entries the RSL holds for the ref. |
| `warnings` | array | Each with a stable `code` and a human `message`. |

Warning codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `no_rsl_entries` | The RSL has no entry for the ref. Coverage may exclude it. |
| `all_entries_skipped` | Every entry for the ref is skipped. |
| `local_ref_missing` | The ref does not exist locally. |
| `local_drift` | The local ref differs from `rsl_tip`. |
| `tag_moved` | A tag has more than one unskipped entry. |
EOF
git add -A && mise run check 2>&1 | grep -E 'issues|ERROR|FAIL|:[0-9]+:[0-9]+' | tail -20

cli: branch and tag commands

branch and tag show what the RSL records for a ref next to the local ref:
the tip the newest unskipped entry records, who pushed it as recorded by
Entire, the asserted time and the signer, then the recent history with
skipped entries marked.

Warnings flag a local ref that differs from the RSL or is missing, a ref
the RSL holds no entries for (its coverage may exclude it), refs whose
every entry is skipped, and tags with more than one unskipped entry,
which were moved.

Names resolve short or in full within each command's namespace through
internal/refresolve, which also implements git's DWIM order for later
commands and fails on ambiguity rather than picking a candidate.

EOF
